mission_01: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), introduced by Finn et al. (2017), is a foundational meta-learning algorithm that learns an initialization of model parameters such that a small number of gradient steps on a new task's support set produces good performance on that task's query set. The key insight is optimizing for fast adaptability rather than direct performance. MAML has two loops: the inner loop adapts parameters θ to task-specific parameters θ' using the support set, and the outer loop updates the meta-parameters θ by computing gradients of the query loss with respect to θ (through the inner loop update). This requires differentiating through the inner loop update, which involves second-order gradients. MAML is model-agnostic — it works with any differentiable model — and has been applied to regression, classification, and reinforcement learning. In this mission, you will implement MAML from scratch using numpy, including sinusoidal task sampling, inner loop adaptation, and outer loop meta-updates.
